newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard to showcase Internet appeal.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard to showcase Internet appeal.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. will on Tuesday roll out its Internet and electronic business technology strategy with leading industry partners helping bolster its image in the fast-growing market, analysts said.

The high technology giant has scheduled a day-long "Electronic Business Strategy" session at a swank San Jose hotel to further position HP as an able provider for major corporate customers seeking to deploy Internet technology.
The meeting comes one day ahead of Hewlett-Packard's semiannual financial analysts' meeting, set behind closed doors on Wednesday at its corporate headquarters here.

But analysts and investors said the main audience for the day-long HP event, dubbed "Creating the Extended Enterprise," is senior executives of the world's top corporations, all potential customers for HP's products and services.

Robert Herwick, president of Herwick Capital Management, said the company is seeking to differentiate its strategy for creating corporate networks known as Intranets, based on Internet technology, from that of its competitors.

"This is HP making everybody comfortable with it, saying: 'yes, it's ok to go ahead and do this now and we're your old friends HP and we've got the right answer for you and so you can go ahead with us,'" Herwick said.

"These enterprises basically have three vendors who they feel comfortable with," he said, saying International Business Machines Corp has an image currently as the choice for real "stick in the muds," while Sun Microsystems Inc had an image of leaving "a lot of product at the door."

By contrast, Hewlett-Packard has outlined a strategy, including new hardware, software and service products unveiled just last month, which incorporates a variety of technologies and stresses that it can help customers integrate them.

It incorporates both the Microsoft Corp Windows NT platform and the Unix operating system, for example, while Sun publicly mocks Microsoft, while IBM has a more complicated rapport with the Redmond, Wash.-based software giant.

And while HP works closely with Microsoft and with its fellow giant PC supplier Intel Corp, which is jointly working with HP to develop the next generation of powerful workstation microprocessors, HP also has a global agreement with Microsoft's Internet software rival, Netscape.

Microsoft Executive Vice President Steve Ballmer, Oracle Corp President Ray Lane, and a senior Netscape Communications Corp executive will all be addressing the conference along with top HP executives.
One theme will be reducing the total cost of ownership of technology, a hot topic at the moment, and the ways in which Internet technology can be used to reduce this.
"They're really going to emphasise the completeness of the solution," said Herwick.
